entities.name: Query asd protein
observations: 338 aa enzyme; predicted molecular mass 36.95 kDa and pI 4.67.
Shows 84.9–85.2% identity over 99.7% coverage to reviewed bacterial aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenases.
Likely functions as a homodimer based on close reviewed homolog annotations.

entities.name: Aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase
observations: EC 1.2.1.11; NADPH-dependent enzyme in the aspartate-family amino-acid biosynthesis pathway.
Catalyzes reductive dephosphorylation of L-aspartyl-4-phosphate to form L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde.
Reviewed homologs annotate NADP/NAD binding and homodimerization.
Participates in lysine, methionine, and threonine biosynthesis.

entities.name: L-aspartyl-4-phosphate reduction
observations: Rhea RHEA:24284; reaction direction represented as L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde + phosphate + NADP(+) = 4-phospho-L-aspartate + NADPH + H(+).
Physiological forward direction is reductive dephosphorylation: 4-phospho-L-aspartate + NADPH + H(+) -> L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde + phosphate + NADP(+).

entities.name: Aspartate-family amino acid biosynthesis
observations: Aspartate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase is the second enzymatic step from L-aspartate toward lysine, methionine, and threonine.
The product L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde is a branch-point intermediate for downstream homoserine and diaminopimelate pathways.
